executive_summary:
Episode 400 (2026-10-08). The host opens by answering Blake Neff, who she says called her names in an X space the day before, and then walks through newly enhanced UVU footage from just before 1:00 p.m. on September 10. According to the host, Blake Neff, Danny Philip, Nate Walker and Mikey McCoy walked with security members Blake Harreff, Blake Gibson and Charlie's driver from behind the Hall of Flags to a lineup of white vehicles she describes as federal, and split into two cars driven by what appear to her to be officers. She says local news footage shows the first group arriving at Timpanogos Hospital at about 1:10 p.m., while the second car, carrying the security members, is not seen arriving, and two of them later return wearing scrubs.

The host says her team has identified Charlie's driver as Christopher Rhoades (she spells it r-h-o-a-d-e-s), says he appears to be from Texas and to work with Brian Harpole, and distinguishes him from a same-named member of TPUSA's new FRG security team. She also names the ICAC officer who she says took Mikey McCoy's statement and says that officer has left her position. She asks viewers for tips on the officer who drove the first group, on Christopher Rhoades and on the fire captain who she says performed CPR at the hospital, saying her team is down to two possibilities.

The second half reads excerpts from Frank Turek's book "The War on Reality" (published, she says, on September 8, 2026). The host contrasts the book's statement that all three men in the back seat tried to stop the bleeding, and that Turek switched to CPR, with Brian Harpole's Shawn Ryan account, notes that the book omits the fire captain named in the independent review, disputes its claim that Dan Flood's team only had jurisdiction over Charlie's immediate area, and compares its account of the surgeon delivering the news with Blake Neff's account of Mikey McCoy as the conduit to Erika Kirk. The episode closes with viewer comments, a clip of Erika Kirk's "grift" slip at AmFest 2025, a Theo Von clip, a merch plug and a riff on Brian Harpole's lawsuit and his phrase "doing the medical".

claims.claim: The host says Blake Neff called her wretched, nasty and absolutely awful in an X space, claimed she dislikes other pretty women, and afterwards called her illiterate on X.
claims.investigative_direction: The X space recording and Blake Neff's subsequent X posts.
claims.transcript_snippet: He said I was wretched, nasty, absolutely awful. Claimed that I dislike other pretty women. He also called me illiterate thereafter on X.

claims.label: Host Questions Why Danny Philip Drove Neff Like an Uber With Neff in the Back Seat
claims.claim: The host says Blake Neff cannot remember what he was doing in Salt Lake City and asks why Danny Philip was driving Neff "like he was in an Uber ride", with Neff in the back seat.
claims.investigative_direction: Rental records for the second Denali and Neff's own account of his travel that day.

claims.label: Host Asks Why Neff and Philip Did Not Drive Straight to the Hospital
claims.claim: The host says she cannot make sense of why Blake Neff and Danny Philip did not immediately drive themselves to the hospital after Charlie was hit.
claims.investigative_direction: UVU footage and phone location data for Neff and Philip between the shot and about 1:00 p.m.
claims.transcript_snippet: one thing that I cannot make sense of is why Blake Neff and Danny Philip didn't just immediately book it to the hospital, to drive themselves over to the hospital.

claims.transcript_snippet: What I'll always remember is the way his lip was quivering, which I'd never seen before, and you you very rarely see from someone that's he was freaking out.

claims.label: In Neff's Clip, Mikey McCoy Called His Father Rob McCoy to Rally Pastors
claims.claim: In the clip, Blake Neff says he called his own mother, and that Mikey McCoy then called his father, Rob McCoy, saying Charlie had been shot and asking him to call all his pastor friends to pray.
claims.investigative_direction: Mikey McCoy's and Rob McCoy's call records for September 10.
claims.transcript_snippet: And around the time I I put that phone away and then he immediately calls his dad. He calls Rob McCoy.

claims.label: In Neff's Clip, Mikey Became "Like a General" Directing People to the Hospital
claims.claim: In the clip, Blake Neff says that after the call Mikey McCoy took "total mastery of himself" and acted "like a general directing a battle", telling people they needed to get to the hospital.
